datasetCard.name: Voyager 1 mission
datasetCard.description: Voyager 1 is a NASA interstellar probe launched on September 5, 1977, designed to explore the outer Solar System and beyond. It conducted flybys of Jupiter (1979) and Saturn (1980), using a gravity assist from Saturn to alter its trajectory out of the ecliptic plane toward interstellar space. The spacecraft carries a 3.7-meter high-gain antenna, imaging systems, infrared and ultraviolet spectrometers, magnetometers, plasma detectors, and cosmic ray instruments, powered by radioisotope thermoelectric generators (RTGs). Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause in August 2012, becoming the first human-made object to enter interstellar space. It continues to transmit heliophysics and plasma data via NASA's Deep Space Network and carries the Golden Record—a curated collection of Earth sounds and images intended for any potential extraterrestrial encounter.

datasetCard.name: Voyager 2 mission
datasetCard.description: Voyager 2 is a NASA interstellar probe launched on August 20, 1977, designed to conduct a Grand Tour of the outer Solar System. It performed close flybys of Jupiter (1979), Saturn (1981), Uranus (1986), and Neptune (1989), remaining the only spacecraft to visit Uranus and Neptune. The probe carries a 3.7-meter high-gain antenna, imaging systems, infrared and ultraviolet spectrometers, magnetometers, plasma detectors, and cosmic ray instruments, powered by radioisotope thermoelectric generators (RTGs). Voyager 2 crossed the heliopause in November 2018, entering interstellar space, and continues to transmit heliophysics and plasma data via NASA's Deep Space Network. Like its twin, it carries the Golden Record—a curated collection of Earth sounds and images intended for any potential extraterrestrial encounter.
